posts.title: Object Lock Buckets on Rustfs for Veeam, Automated With Ansible
posts.description: In the previous post I have installed RustFS on a dedicated VM, from the data disk and the systemd service to TLS and the rc client. The server is running, but it is still empty. In this post I will create the buckets, automate their creation and their access keys with an Ansible playbook, and test the different combinations of immutability.

posts.title: Replacing Minio in My Home Lab With Rustfs
posts.description: I’ve been using MinIO as the S3 object storage behind my Veeam lab for a while. After its license changes and the archiving of the community repository, I started looking for a replacement and found RustFS : an S3-compatible object storage written in Rust and released under the Apache 2.0 license, with support for versioning and Object Lock. posts.title: Veeam Malware Tester: Test and Demonstrate Veeam Malware Detection Capabilities
posts.description: Testing Veeam’s malware detection features requires a specific set of conditions that may be hard to reproduce quickly in a production or demo environment. To solve this, I created a script for Linux systems that allows you to quickly create a series of harmless artifacts to trigger each of the three detection engines included in Veeam Backup & Replication (VBR): File System Analysis, Inline Entro
